# Library sound restoration upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Ruby 2.7.0p0.
Dependencies: Ruby standard library. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

Environment.call/bind provides a synchronous source embedding: listen(file
 token, callback token) returns a subscription, start can invoke it before
returning, and unlisten may reenter navigation. decode(file token, packet,
completion token) returns {deferred:false,frame} or {deferred:true}. Deferred
completion invokes the bound native closure on an explicit later host turn.
Transport receives a physical cancellation observer corresponding to the
native attempt state; cancel is idempotent. The wire embedding interns file
objects and forwards source/sink calls. Go uses context cancellation; the other
native ports use object flags. No native DOM/Promise runtime is claimed.

# Preservation sessions use block observers and distinct Struct visits.
Visit=Struct.new(:id,:file,:handle,:received,:displayed,:generation)
module Cancellation
 def cancel
  return if @aborted
  @aborted=true;@stop.call;@env.call('cancel',@file['token'],@number)
 end
end
class Attempt
 include Cancellation
 attr_reader :file,:number,:aborted
 def initialize(env,file,number,active=-> {1},audit=->(f){},view=->(f,o){})
  @env,@file,@number,@aborted=env,file,number,false;@stop=->{}
  yield self if block_given?
  env.call('transport',file['token'],number)
  if file['feed'] && !@aborted
   callback=env.bind(->(packet){
    next if @aborted
    order=active.call;
    next unless order
    deliver=->(frame){ audit.call(frame);view.call(frame,order)}
    value=env.call('decode',file['token'],packet,env.bind(deliver));deliver.call(value['frame']) unless value['deferred']
   })
   subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)
   removed=false
   @stop=-> {unless removed;removed=true;env.call('unlisten',file['token'],subscription);end}
   if @aborted;@stop.call;else;env.call('start',file['token']);end
  end
 end
end
class Session
 def initialize(env);@env=env;@visit=nil;@serial=0;@attempts=0;@tasks={};@disposed=false;end
 def current(v);@visit.equal?(v);end
 def enqueue(v,kind)
  v.generation=(v.generation||0)+1;generation=v.generation
  @attempts+=1;n=@attempts;entry={fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,visitId:v.id,kind:kind};;@env.call('record',entry)
  h=Attempt.new(@env,v.file,n,
   ->{if current(v) && v.generation==generation;v.received=(v.received||0)+1;end},
   ->(frame){@env.call('recordProgress',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,frame:frame})},
   ->(frame,order){
    if current(v) && order>(v.displayed||0)
     v.displayed=order
     @env.call('showProgress',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,frame:frame})
    end
   }) do |attempt|
    @tasks[n]=attempt
    v.handle=attempt if current(v) && v.generation==generation
   end
  h.cancel unless current(v) && v.generation==generation
  h
 end
 def notice(v,h);;@env.call('showQueued',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:h.number,visitId:v.id,status:'queued'});end
 def release(v);h=v.handle;v.handle=nil;h.cancel if h;end
 def select(file)
  return nil if @disposed
  @serial+=1;request=@serial;old=@visit;@visit=nil;release(old) if old
  return nil if @disposed||@serial!=request
  v=Visit.new(request,file,nil);@visit=v;h=enqueue(v,'select');notice(v,h) if current(v)&&v.handle.equal?(h);h
 end
 def retry
  v=@visit;return nil if !v||!v.handle||@disposed
  release(v)
  accepted=v;h=enqueue(accepted,'retry');notice(accepted,h) if current(accepted)&&accepted.handle.equal?(h);h
 end
 def hide;@serial+=1;old=@visit;@visit=nil;release(old) if old;end
 def dispose;return if @disposed;@disposed=true;hide;@tasks.each_value(&:cancel);end
 def snapshot;v=@visit;{visitId:v ? v.id : nil,fileId:v ? v.file['id'] : nil,attemptId:v&&v.handle ? v.handle.number : nil,disposed:@disposed,attempts:@attempts};end
end

class Telemetry
 attr_reader :stop
 def initialize(env,file)
  callback=env.bind(->(packet){deliver=->(frame){env.call('recordDelta',frame)};value=env.call('decode',file['token'],packet,env.bind(deliver));deliver.call(value['frame']) unless value['deferred']})
  env.call('start',file['token']);subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)
  @stop=->{env.call('unlisten',file['token'],subscription)}
 end
end

forbidden_effects: Missing cached initial panel progress because listening begins after start.

Treating numeric loaded values as a monotonic freshness measure.

lifecycle_identity: Each selection creates a distinct visit, including selection of the identical file object.
Retry creates a new physical attempt within the existing visit.
Progress audit remains associated with the file and attempt that accepted the packet; visible progress belongs to its originating visit.
The progress source is shared across attempts and visits for a file; file object identity, id, and size are stable.
Attempt numbering and disposal state belong to each Session instance.

obligations.text: Make the panel subscription available before starting a source that can synchronously emit cached packets, while preserving later streaming and subsequent source reuse.
Retain audit recording for each accepted packet when decoding completes, immediately or later, including completion after its visit closes or its attempt is canceled.
Publish a decoded frame only while its originating visit remains current. Recheck eligibility after recordProgress, because that synchronous host callback can navigate.
Order panel frames by packet reception rather than decode completion or numeric loaded value. Once a newer frame has been displayed in a visit, an older completion must not replace it.

Support retirement during synchronous startup before the caller receives the cleanup handle: prevent further packet admission by the retired subscription, retain accepted audit work, and clean up the eventual retired resources.

Preserve newer navigation through callback-capable cleanup. Retire captured old ownership before cancellation and prevent an outer operation from overwriting resources installed by reentrant navigation.

Preserve retry acceptance behavior: cancel the prior handle before enqueueing, then enqueue and record exactly one retry for the captured visit even if cancellation navigates. Cancel the resulting handle if that visit is no longer current, and emit its queued notice only while it is current.
Preserve synchronous queue recording before transfer construction, existing queue and notice fields, attempt numbering, transport calls, and cancellation behavior.
Preserve listener-removal commitment before detach callbacks, inert repeated removal, idempotent cancellation and disposal, disposal of tracked transfers, and independence between workspaces.
Keep the Telemetry consumer's existing live delta behavior and public source/sink interfaces unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Panel reception must be installed before start can emit cached packets.
Capture packet ordering and originating identity before invoking decode, which can complete immediately or later.
Audit accepted decoding before attempting visible publication; recheck current-visit eligibility after the audit callback.
Prevent older publication after a newer frame is displayed, including reentrant publication through synchronous host callbacks.
Clear current old-visit ownership before callback-capable cancellation; recheck the selection request after old cleanup.
A retry cancels its previous handle before its retained enqueue operation.
Record the queue entry before constructing the corresponding Attempt.
Commit listener removal before invoking the host detach callback.
preservation: Ordinary streaming, subsequent uses, transport creation, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, and queue-record behavior.
Accepted decoding survives physical listener removal; cancellation does not retroactively remove retained history.
Existing queue records contain exactly fileId, attemptId, visitId, and kind; notices contain fileId, attemptId, visitId, and status set to queued.
Current-visit display eligibility is distinct from attempt cancellation: accepted work is not automatically made invisible merely because retry canceled its attempt.
Full frames replace displayed state and may decrease or reset loaded values.
Telemetry retains its existing start-before-listen sequence and recordDelta behavior.
scope: Draft contract for restoring initial panel progress and preventing stale decoded frames from rolling back its display in src/workflow.rb.
